target_customer: Small and marginal Indian farmers selling produce, and businesses buying agricultural produce directly
problem: Farmers sold through local mandi auctions and middlemen who set prices and added cost; Kisan Network connected farmers directly to buyers and ran the produce from farm to buyer.
business_model: Agricultural produce supply chain with a transaction commission (TechCrunch 2016 reported no more than 8% per transaction)
product_category: Agtech marketplace and supply chain, India

founders.name: Aditya Agarwalla
education: Princeton University, computer science, dropped out (started Kisan Network as an undergraduate thesis project)
founders.background_notes: Thiel Fellow (the Thiel Foundation's $100,000 award per Business Insider and AgFunder coverage).

founders.name: Sanjay Agarwalla
prior_employers: Distributor for major Western brands in India (TechCrunch 2016)
founders.background_notes: Father of Aditya. YC page also lists him as co-founder of Mera Gaon.

exit.reason: YC lists the company as inactive; no shutdown report or statement was found.

competitors.name: Ninjacart
competitors.what: Bengaluru B2B marketplace connecting farmers and brands to retailers
competitors.traction_then: Over 400 retail stores and restaurants in Bangalore and about Rs 4 crore monthly revenue by June 2016
competitors.funding_then: $3M Series A led by Accel in March 2016

competitors.name: Local mandi auctions and middlemen
competitors.what: The traditional channel where produce was auctioned and brokers set prices
competitors.traction_then: Dominant incumbent channel per TechCrunch and the YC launch post

technical_complexity.rationale: An Android app, farmer listings and a back-office portal are standard engineering; the hard part was physical logistics, field operations and quality grading across villages.

defensibility.rationale: Farmer relationships and village ambassadors build some stickiness but buyers and farmers could use other channels, and logistics operations are capital hungry.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed Kisan Network; Ninjacart scaled with Tiger Global and Walmart funding while Kisan raised $3M in 2020.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in March 2016 described farmers losing price and bearing transport cost through mandis and middlemen and quoted a farmer saying the service gave better prices. India's farm supply chain is fragmented; no volume data was given.

branding.name_origin: Kisan Network means 'Farmer Network' in Hindi, per a 2015 Princeton independent work report that describes the project.

identity.logo: App icon seen in press; design not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Farmer-centric and plain; founders quoted 'Farmers could not care less how much we have raised'.

branding.brand_signature: Princeton dorm project to Thiel Fellow story of a father and son, covered by National Geographic
branding.community_and_virality: Story coverage in TechCrunch, National Geographic, Forbes and Economic Times per the YC page; no community or merch signal.

brand_strength.rationale: Good founder-story press but a generic Hindi descriptive name and little evidence the brand drove adoption among farmers.

outcome_analysis: Kisan Network began as a Princeton project, joined YC in Winter 2016 and reached about 55,000 farmers in 6,000 villages with a team of 75 before raising a $3M seed in January 2020 led by Mistletoe. YC lists it as inactive, but no shutdown report, cause or later funding was found, so failure factors are left empty. Low-margin produce logistics and the 2020 pandemic disrupted Indian agri supply chains, but no source ties those to this company.
notes: The January 2020 round is called a $3M seed by Inc42 and DealStreetAsia headlines; AgFunder does not label it. It is confirmed by Inc42, AgFunder and Business Insider India. The YC and Thiel amounts for 2016 rest on CB Insights (YC $120K, seen only in search results) and Business Insider (Thiel $100K); one aggregator lists total raised as $3.6M. Founded year is uncertain: sources give 2015 to 2016, the Princeton thesis dates to 2015. Website kisannetwork.com returned only a tagline ('Smart Deals in Your Hand'). Not to be confused with KisanKonnect. Confidence high is claimed on founders, competition and funding all being sourced, though the competitor list is thin.
